transcript.answer: At most three upkeep runs can start per repository for one event (a push to main). Priority goes to the pull request upkept longest ago. A pull request that has never been upkept goes first. Next comes the one whose newest upkeep run started earliest, and then the oldest pull request. Before the 2026-10-25 change, the three oldest pull requests always won. When those three kept failing, they took every start on every push and starved the rest.

judgements.reason: The answer states the limit of three per event per repository and the full priority order (never upkept, then earliest newest upkeep run, then oldest), with extra historical detail that does not contradict the gold.
